searchDocs.title: Why does this library exist?​
searchDocs.content: This library is designed for fast iteration and small to medium sized games!  I made it because I didn't want to search through folders to find the sound I wanted. I had to write multiple lines just to go fetch a sound, and I found it annoying. On top of that, if the sound's location changed or the sound didn't exist anymore, the entire block would error. So, of course, I spent over 100 hours trying to fix that with a library, as that's completely logical!!!

searchDocs.title: How far does it scale?​
searchDocs.content: It also works in larger games without much issue. The only bottleneck is that it becomes less convenient after a certain number of sounds. There is no hierarchy when fetching sounds; it is completely flat. So the difficulty of giving every sound a unique name goes up as the number of sounds goes up.  The Extension has a limit of 800 sounds, as that should be a safe number for a language server to handle without errors. The library itself should handle a few thousand sounds with no problem if you don't care for the extension.

searchDocs.title: Working with the library​
searchDocs.content: Set your sounds up in Studio for their most common use. Adjust each sound in edit mode, then use presets or change properties yourself for the small things that differ at runtime. If a sound ends up too different from its original copy, it may be better to make a new Sound, even if it has the same SoundId. Sounds should not decide your business logic, at least 95% of the time. Sounds should go on top of your code, not mold it.

searchDocs.title: Memory optimizations​
searchDocs.content: Optimizing may be important if your game needs to run on phones or old devices.  In short:  Only preload the sounds that you know need it.Lazy load your sounds wherever possible.Destroy sounds when you don't need them for the moment.Use third party software like Audacity or FL Studio to compress your audio.

searchDocs.title: Preloading​
searchDocs.content: This library makes preloading easy, as you just need to tag a sound with VluxySF_Preload. But just because it's easy, that doesn't mean you should preload everything, especially if your game uses more than 20 sounds. The more sounds you preload, the more memory is taken up throughout the game.  warning There is no way to undo preloading a sound.  If a sound only has to be ready for a while, like the sounds of one map, warm it instead. You can chill it again once you are done.

searchDocs.title: Lazy loading​
searchDocs.content: Lazy loading is when you only create an object when it's needed. This library makes that easy, as you just need to call VluxySF.Fetch.  Just make sure you call that function right when you need the sound, and there you go!

searchDocs.title: Destroying your sounds​
searchDocs.content: If you want to save more memory, destroy the sound made by VluxySF once you're done playing it. VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce does this for you automatically.  note Lazy loading and destroying only save memory if the SoundId was not preloaded and no other sound with the same SoundId exists.

searchDocs.title: Sound editing​
searchDocs.content: Editing your audio files should be a last resort, as it is the most tedious of these methods. There is also a monthly import limit for audio in Roblox. But this is the best way to save memory, if it's worth it to you.

searchDocs.title: When to optimize?​
searchDocs.content: It depends on the project. In most cases, if your codebase is designed well, or well enough, it can be done later down the line.  For instance, maybe you're just polishing your game up. That could be the best time to start optimizing your sound memory, if it's needed.  But of course, only optimize when you need to, and if you need to!

searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: You put your Sounds inside a Configuration named SOUNDS in ServerStorage.When the server starts, VluxySF reads every Sound and turns it into a lightweight definition. All the definitions together are called the schema.The schema is shared with every client, so both sides can create any sound on demand from its name.  Because only definitions are stored, a Sound instance exists only while you are using it. That keeps memory low, and you can still preload the few sounds that have to be ready instantly.

searchDocs.title: Set it up​
searchDocs.content: Follow these pages in order and you will have sounds playing in a few minutes:  Installation: add the package with Wally.Folder Setup: build your SOUNDS Configuration in Studio.Initialization: start the library on the server and the client.Examples: fetch, play, and adjust your sounds.

searchDocs.title: Go further​
searchDocs.content: Extension: get autocomplete and type checking for your sound names in VS Code.Advice: tips on using the library well and keeping sound memory low.API Docs: every function, with examples.

searchDocs.title: 1. Add the package​
searchDocs.content: If your project does not use Wally yet, run wally init in your project directory first.  Then add VluxySF under [dependencies] in your wally.toml:  [package] name = "your_name/your_project" version = "0.1.0" registry = "https://github.com/UpliftGames/wally-index" realm = "shared" [dependencies] VluxySF = "greenviper126/vluxysf@^1"   Run wally install in your project. Wally creates a Packages folder that contains VluxySF.

searchDocs.title: 2. Sync the package into Studio​
searchDocs.content: VluxySF runs on both the server and the client, so the Packages folder has to be somewhere both can reach. ReplicatedStorage is the usual place.  Add the Packages folder to your Rojo project file:  { "name": "your_project", "tree": { "$className": "DataModel", "ReplicatedStorage": { "$className": "ReplicatedStorage", "Packages": { "$path": "Packages" } } } }

searchDocs.title: 3. Require it​
searchDocs.content: With the setup above, you can require the library from any script:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF)   Every example in these docs uses this path. If your Packages folder is somewhere else, change the path to match.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: The library needs sounds to work with. Continue to Folder Setup.

searchDocs.title: ToDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Conversions.ToDefinition( sound: Sound -- The Sound to convert. ) → SoundDefinition-- The resulting SoundDefinition. Converts a Sound into a SoundDefinition. local mySound = ... local soundDefinition = VluxySF.Conversions.ToDefinition(mySound) print(soundDefinition)

searchDocs.title: FromDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Conversions.FromDefinition( definition: SoundDefinition-- The SoundDefinition to convert. ) → Sound -- The resulting Sound. Converts a SoundDefinition into a Sound. local soundDefinition = { Properties = { Name = "MySound", SoundId = "rbxassetid://123456789", Volume = 0.5, SoundGroup = "GAME", }, Effects = {}, EffectCount = 0 } local mySound = VluxySF.Conversions.FromDefinition(soundDefinition) mySound:Play()

searchDocs.title: Setup​
searchDocs.content: Install the Extension in VS Code.Get the Plugin into Roblox Studio: Extension 0.5.0 or newer: the extension installs the plugin for you as a local plugin and keeps it up to date. Restart Roblox Studio when the extension says the plugin was installed.Older versions: install the Plugin from the Creator Store yourself. Make sure the port matches in the extension and the plugin. By default it is 7842.Click the VluxySF icon in the Plugins tab of Studio. You should hear a connect sound.  If it stays connected, you are ready to bake your types.  warning If you update the extension to 0.5.0 or newer, remove the Creator Store plugin in Studio's plugin manager. Otherwise two copies of the plugin will run.

searchDocs.title: How it works​
searchDocs.content: The companion software bakes types for you. More specifically, it makes a union of string literals out of every sound name under your SOUNDS Configuration.  The plugin reads the sound names in Studio and sends them to the extension. The extension then writes them into a small file inside the VluxySF package named _vluxysf_sound_name_types.luau. The library uses that type for the name argument of its fetch functions.  By default, the file looks like this:  --!strict export type GeneratedSoundNames = string return nil   Once baked, it looks like this:  --!strict export type GeneratedSoundNames = "A Cure for All" | "Agaiiiiiin" | "Bubble Pop Parade" | "Clara OL" | ... return nil   With the Loose Name Types setting turned on in the extension, any other string is allowed too:  --!strict export type GeneratedSoundNames = string | "A Cure for All" | "Agaiiiiiin" | "Bubble Pop Parade" | "Clara OL" | ... return nil   note This extension has a limit of 800 sounds for type baking! That should be a safe number for a language server to handle without errors.

searchDocs.title: Recommended editor setup​
searchDocs.content: It is highly recommended that you use Luau-LSP as your language server.  tip If you use Luau-LSP, make sure Enable Fragment AutoComplete is off. At the moment (2/28/2026) it stops inline suggestions from popping up most of the time.

searchDocs.title: SetMainVolume​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundGroups.SetMainVolume( mainVolume: number-- Volume level to set. ) → () Sets the volume of the main SoundGroup that all other groups derive from. VluxySF.Groups.SetMainVolume(0.3)

searchDocs.title: SetVolumes​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundGroups.SetVolumes( mainVolume: number?,-- -- Main volume level to set. volumes: {[string]: number}-- Dictionary of the volumes to adjust. ) → () Sets Volumes to the provided levels. TIP MainVolume and the individual volume elements are optional when using SoundGroups.SetVolumes. local mainVolume = 1 local volumes = { ["GAME"] = 0.7, ["UI"] = 0.5, } VluxySF.Groups.SetVolumes(mainVolume, volumes)

searchDocs.title: The basics​
searchDocs.content: Legend:  ⚙️ = Configuration Instance 📁 = Folder Instance 🔊 = Sound Instance   Example:  SOUNDS⚙️ ← The base Configuration ├─ MUSIC⚙️ ← Becomes the MUSIC SoundGroup │ ├─ mainTheme🔊 ← Grouped to MUSIC │ └─ battle🔊 ← Grouped to MUSIC └─ SFX⚙️ ← Becomes the SFX SoundGroup ├─ click🔊 ← Grouped to SFX └─ explosion🔊 ← Grouped to SFX   There are only three rules:  Every direct child of SOUNDS is a Configuration. Each one becomes a SoundGroup with the same name. A Folder or Sound placed directly under SOUNDS throws an error on startup.Every Sound goes inside one of those group Configurations. It is assigned to that SoundGroup automatically.Every Sound has a unique name. The name is the key you fetch it with, like VluxySF.Fetch("explosion"). If two sounds share a name, a warning appears at runtime and only one of them is kept.

searchDocs.title: Naming conventions​
searchDocs.content: Instance	Recommended	Required?SoundGroup Configurations	UPPER_CASE	No, any name works Folders	PascalCase	No, any name works Sounds	PascalCase or camelCase	No, but the name must be unique

searchDocs.title: Organizing with folders​
searchDocs.content: Inside a group you can use Folders (📁) however you like.  SOUNDS⚙️ └─ SFX⚙️ ├─ UI📁 │ └─ click🔊 └─ Game📁 └─ explosion🔊   tip The hierarchy inside a group does not affect the library. Sounds are always fetched by name, so you can reorganize your folders at any time without touching your code.

searchDocs.title: Preloading sounds​
searchDocs.content: Want certain sounds to be ready instantly? Give a Sound or a Folder the tag VluxySF_Preload, and it is preloaded as soon as the client starts.  Tag a Sound to preload that one sound.Tag a Folder to preload every sound inside it.  SOUNDS⚙️ ├─ MUSIC⚙️ │ ├─ mainTheme🔊 │ └─ battles📁 ← Tagged "VluxySF_Preload": both sounds inside preload │ ├─ importantSound1🔊 │ └─ importantSound2🔊 └─ SFX⚙️ ├─ click🔊 └─ explosions📁 ├─ commonExplosion🔊 ← Tagged "VluxySF_Preload": only this sound preloads └─ uncommonLongExplosion🔊   You can add a tag in Studio from the Tags section at the bottom of the Properties window.  warning Only preload the sounds that need it. A preloaded sound stays in memory for the whole session, and there is no way to undo it. See Advice for more.

searchDocs.title: Preload timeout​
searchDocs.content: The client waits for the tagged sounds to preload before it continues. You can pass a timeout (in seconds) to InitClient. If preloading takes longer than that, the client continues and the sounds keep loading in the background. The default is 5 seconds.  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local preloadTimeout = 10 VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(preloadTimeout) -- Reaches this line once the sounds are preloaded or the timeout is reached.

searchDocs.title: Configuring sounds​
searchDocs.content: Set up each Sound in Studio exactly how you want it to play.  Properties: Set SoundId, Volume, PlaybackSpeed, and so on directly on the Sound. Every property is kept except for the Parent.Effects: Add effects such as EqualizerSoundEffect or ReverbSoundEffect as children of the Sound.  note Only SoundEffects are kept. Any other instance parented to a Sound is skipped with a warning.Only one effect of each class is kept per Sound.A fetched effect is named after its class, so you can always reach it with sound.EchoSoundEffect, whatever it was called in Studio.

searchDocs.title: End result​
searchDocs.content: When you are done, your SOUNDS Configuration should look something like this in Studio:    note The SOUNDS Configuration belongs in ServerStorage. Making it a direct child of that service is recommended.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: Your sounds are ready. Continue to Initialization to start the library.

searchDocs.title: Default​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Default( center: number,-- The central value around which the jitter will occur. spread: number-- The maximum deviation from the center value. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Standard Jitter function that randomly varies from the center value +- the spread. local myJitter = Jitter.Default(1, 0.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random value.

searchDocs.title: Range​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Range( min: number,-- The minimum value for the jitter range. max: number-- The maximum value for the jitter range. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Essentially just a random number that requires a specified range. local myJitter = Jitter.Range(0.85, 1.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random value.

searchDocs.title: Scale​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.Scale( spread: number-- The maximum deviation from the center value. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Very similar to Jitter.Default but the center value is 1. local myJitter = Jitter.Scale(0.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random value.

searchDocs.title: UnitLog​
searchDocs.content: </> Jitter.UnitLog( center: number,-- The central value around which the jitter will occur. spread: number-- The maximum deviation from the center value. ) → () → number-- Generates the jitter value when called. Produces jitter values with a shaped distribution that favors the center value. local myJitter = Jitter.UnitLog(1, 0.15) local sound1 = ... sound1.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets a random shaped value. local sound2 = ... sound2.PlaybackSpeed = myJitter() -- Sets another random shaped value. TIP This can be used to make more natural repetitious sounds like footsteps.

searchDocs.title: Fetch​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.Fetch( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the sound. preset: (Sound ) → ()?-- Preset to apply. ) → Sound -- The fetched sound instance. Finds the specified SoundDefinition and gives back a Sound. If somthing goes wrong a Blank Sound is returned instead. INFO If a sound is Preloaded it is instead Cloned from the preloadFolder If a sound is Warmed it is instead Cloned from the warmed cache. WARNING If the sound is not preloaded or warmed it may take a moment to fetch and load as it needs to be created first. local mySound = VluxySF.Fetch("MySound") mySound.Volume = 0.3 local echoEffect = mySound.EchoSoundEffect if echoEffect then echoEffect.WetLevel = 1.3 end mySound:Play()

searchDocs.title: FetchStrict​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.FetchStrict( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: (Sound ) → ()?-- Preset to apply. ) → Sound? -- The fetched Sound instance if success. Similar to VluxySF.Fetch but will not return a Blank Sound on fail. local mySound = VluxySF.Fetch("MySound") if mySound then mySound.Volume = 0.3 local echoEffect = mySound.EchoSoundEffect if echoEffect then echoEffect.WetLevel = 1.3 end mySound:Play() end

searchDocs.title: FetchPlayOnce​
searchDocs.content: RequiresSchema </> VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce( name: string,-- The name of the Sound. parent: Instance? ,-- Parent of the Sound. preset: (Sound ) → ()?,-- Preset to apply. waitOnLoad: boolean?-- Wait for the Sound to load? Always separate thread. ) → () → ()-- Cleanup function. Plays a OneShot Sound and cleans up after playing. VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("MySound")

searchDocs.title: SoundSchema​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundSchema { SoundGroupContainer: SoundGroup -- Main SoundGroup for all other SoundGroups. SoundGroups: SoundGroups-- Dictionary of SoundGroups under the Main SoundGroup. UnattachedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Un-Parented Sounds. WarmedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Warmed Sounds. PreloadedSounds: Configuration -- Configuration for Preloaded Sounds. SoundDefinitions: SoundDefinitions-- Dictionary of SoundDefinitions. PreloadIds: {string}-- List of sound names to Preload. } The Schema for the library that is shared on client and server.

searchDocs.content: </> Schema.Get() → SoundSchema-- The internal sound schema used by the system. The full Schema used internally by the library. print(VluxySF.Schema.Get())

searchDocs.title: GetDefinitions​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetDefinitions() → SoundDefinitions-- All converted sound data Returns all SoundDefinitions in the Schema. print(VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinitions())

searchDocs.title: GetDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetDefinition( definitionName: string-- The name of the sound definition to retrieve. ) → SoundDefinition?-- The SoundDefinition associated with the provided name. Retrieves a SoundDefinition from the Schema based on its name. print(VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinition("MySound"))

searchDocs.title: GetNames​
searchDocs.content: </> Schema.GetNames() → {string}-- All registered sound names. Returns all sound names in the library. print(VluxySF.Schema.GetNames())

searchDocs.title: Get​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Get() → {[string]: Sound }-- The current sounds being Warmed. Returns a hash of the current sounds that are warmed. print(VluxySF.Cache.Get())

searchDocs.title: IsWarmed​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.IsWarmed( soundName: string-- Name of the Sound. ) → boolean-- Is that sound warmed? Tells you if a sound from its name is currently warmed. print(VluxySF.Cache.IsWarmed("MySound"))

searchDocs.title: Warm​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Warm( ...: string-- Names of the Sounds. ) → () Loads the Sound to the Client. If the the same Sound is fetched it will instead Clone from it. WARNING You should only warm if you need a sound to play without a delay or to play without fail but dont plan to constantly use it. TIP You can Warm at the top of a script or a seperate script if the sound you play is in a connection or function that gets called later. Some examples include loading a map and its sounds in. Maybe warming the sounds when first loading the map is a good idea!? VluxySF.Cache.Warm("MySound") --now if its used later on it should be ready to play. --do stuff task.wait(5) --do stuff VluxySF.FetchplayOnce("MySound") --should play without delay now

searchDocs.title: Chill​
searchDocs.content: </> Cache.Chill( ...: string-- Names of the Sounds. ) → () If a Sound with that name is currently warmed it is removed it from the cache. INFO Removing a sound from the cache does not garentee that it will be unloaded. If you still have Sounds with the same Id it will still be in memmory. VluxySF.Cache.Warm("MySound") local onPlay = Instance.new("BindableEvent") local myWarmedSound = ... local function playSound() myWarmedSound:Play() --plays without delay end OnPlay.Event:Connect(playSound) OnPlay.Destroying:Connect(function() myWarmedSound:Destroy() --clean up our sound VluxySF.Cache.Chill("MySound") -- now the sound isn't warmed end) --Now if OnPlay is destroyed it wont be warmed anymore. --So, if the soundId isnt used anywhere else it will be removed from memmory.

searchDocs.title: InitServer​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Startup.InitServer( soundFolder: Configuration -- The SOUNDS Configurartion. ) → () Injects the SOUNDS Configuration into the library and creates the Schema. INFO It compiles all the information into Folders, Configurations, Sounds, SoundGroups, and sounds names to Preload. The schema is locked once Start.InitServer runs. Meaning you cannot add new Sounds, SoundGroups, etc... to the library. DANGER This should only run once! local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.VluxySF) local soundConfig = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild("SOUNDS") VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(soundConfig)

searchDocs.title: InitClient​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.InitClient( timeout: number?-- Timeout for waiting on sounds to preload. ) → () Fetches the Schema from the server and preloads all sounds that require it. DANGER This should only run once! local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.VluxySF) local timeout = 4 VluxySF.Startup.InitClient(timeout)

searchDocs.title: IsInitialized​
searchDocs.content: </> Startup.IsInitialized() → boolean-- Is initialized? Checks if the sound schema has been initialized. print(VluxySF.Startup.IsInitialized())

searchDocs.title: WaitForSchema​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Startup.WaitForSchema() → () Waits until the sound schema is initialized and ready for use. INFO If you know that your code will execute after the Schema is loaded then this is not needed. local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.WaitForSchema() --yields VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("MySound")

searchDocs.title: ConnectForSchema​
searchDocs.content: </> Startup.ConnectForSchema( finished: () → ()-- Callback function to execute when the schema is created. ) → () → ()-- Cleanup function. Alternative to Startup.WaitForSchema if you do not want to pause the current block. local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.ConnectForSchema(function() VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("MySound") end) --doesn't yield down here!

searchDocs.title: Fetch​
searchDocs.content: This is the main function of the library! It rebuilds your sound on request and always gives you a Sound.  local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("LoFiBeat1") -- Always returns a Sound. -- Do stuff here / adjust properties. sound:Play()   If the sound cannot be found, a warning appears and a blank Sound is returned instead, so your code keeps running.

searchDocs.title: FetchStrict​
searchDocs.content: Use FetchStrict if you would rather get nil than a blank Sound when something goes wrong.  local sound = VluxySF.FetchStrict("LoFiBeat1") -- Can return nil. if sound then -- Do stuff here / adjust properties. sound:Play() end

searchDocs.title: FetchPlayOnce​
searchDocs.content: If you just need a one shot, FetchPlayOnce fetches the sound, plays it once, and destroys it when it ends.  VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("LoFiBeat1")   It returns a cleanup function that you can call to stop and destroy the sound early:  local stopSound = VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("LongExplosion1") task.wait(1) stopSound()

searchDocs.title: Choosing a parent​
searchDocs.content: The second argument of every fetch function is the parent. Give it a BasePart or an Attachment to play the sound in 3D space.  local door = workspace.Door VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("DoorCreak1", door) -- Plays from the door.   info A sound that is fetched without a parent is placed in a Configuration named UnattachedSounds inside SoundService. It stays there until you destroy it, so call sound:Destroy() once you are done with a sound you fetched yourself.

searchDocs.title: Presets​
searchDocs.content: A preset is a function that receives the Sound and changes it. Pass one as the third argument of a fetch function to set up the sound the same way every time.  local presets = VluxySF.Presets -- Combine lets you merge multiple presets into one. local myPreset = presets.Combine( presets.NaturalVolumeJitter(0.8, 0.12), presets.NaturalPlaybackJitter(0.7, 0.09), presets.Parent(workspace) ) VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("RandomSound1", nil, myPreset) task.delay(0.1, function() VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("RandomSound1", nil, myPreset) end) -- This sound should use the same preset, but with a different parent. local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("RandomSound1", workspace.CurrentCamera, myPreset) -- This sound is different, but it should play in a similar way. local otherSound = VluxySF.Fetch("OtherRandomSound1", nil, myPreset)

searchDocs.title: Making your own presets​
searchDocs.content: A preset is any function that takes a Sound. Wrap it in another function when it needs settings:  local function randomName(name: string): (Sound) -> () return function(sound: Sound) sound.Name = name .. math.random() end end local myPreset = VluxySF.Presets.Combine( randomName("Footstep"), VluxySF.Presets.Volume(0.6) ) local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("Footstep1", nil, myPreset)   tip You can keep your own presets in a module and use them just like the built in ones.  note Combined presets are applied in order, from the first argument to the last.It is recommended that you only use presets to set properties and do similar one time work.

searchDocs.title: Jitter​
searchDocs.content: The jitter presets above are built from VluxySF.Jitter, which you can also use on its own. A jitter is a function that gives you a slightly different number each time you call it.  local pitchJitter = VluxySF.Jitter.UnitLog(1, 0.15) -- Stays close to 1. local function playFootstep() local sound = VluxySF.Fetch("Footstep1") sound.PlaybackSpeed = pitchJitter() sound:Play() end   Jitter.UnitLog favors values near the center, which makes repeated sounds like footsteps feel more natural. See the Jitter API for the other kinds.

searchDocs.title: SoundGroups​
searchDocs.content: Every group Configuration in your SOUNDS Configuration becomes a SoundGroup, and all of them sit under one main SoundGroup. That gives you a main volume and a volume for each group.  Volumes can be set on the server or the client. The client is recommended for player settings.  local mainVolume = 0.8 local groupVolumes = { GAME = 0.7, MUSIC = 0.55, SFX = 0.64, } local function onSettingsChanged() -- Do stuff here if you want, like clamping your values. A SoundGroup volume can go from 0 to 10. VluxySF.Groups.SetVolumes(mainVolume, groupVolumes) end onSettingsChanged()   tip Call this whenever a slider or setting changes to update the volumes live.  note The main volume is optional. Pass nil to leave it as it is.You only need to list the groups you want to change.There are more functions for working with your SoundGroups. See the SoundGroups API.

searchDocs.title: Keeping sounds ready​
searchDocs.content: A sound that is fetched for the first time has to be created and loaded, which can take a moment. On the client, there are two ways to have a sound ready before you need it.

searchDocs.title: Preload​
searchDocs.content: A preloaded sound stays loaded for the whole session. The easiest way is to tag it in Studio, but you can also preload by name at runtime:  VluxySF.Preload.Selected("BossTheme1", "BossRoar1") -- Yields until they are loaded.

searchDocs.title: Warm and chill​
searchDocs.content: Warming keeps a sound loaded only for as long as you need it. Warm it before the moment it matters, and chill it afterwards to let it go.  VluxySF.Cache.Warm("BossTheme1", "BossRoar1") -- Ready to play without a delay. -- Later, during the boss fight. VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("BossRoar1") -- The fight is over, so these sounds are not needed anymore. VluxySF.Cache.Chill("BossTheme1", "BossRoar1")   note Preload and Cache only work on the client.Chilling a sound does not unload it while other sounds with the same SoundId still exist.  See Advice for when to use each one.

searchDocs.title: Reading the schema​
searchDocs.content: You can read what the library knows about your sounds at any time.  print(VluxySF.Schema.GetNames()) -- Every sound name. print(VluxySF.Schema.GetDefinition("LoFiBeat1")) -- The stored properties and effects of one sound. print(VluxySF.Groups.GetNames()) -- Every SoundGroup name.

searchDocs.title: 1. Start the server​
searchDocs.content: In a server script, give the library your SOUNDS Configuration:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) -- The Configuration that holds the sounds you want to use. local soundFolder = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild("SOUNDS") VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(soundFolder) -- The schema can be used from here on.   info InitServer reads every sound into the schema and then destroys the SOUNDS Configuration in the running game to save memory. Your Configuration in Studio is not changed. The schema is locked once it is created, so sounds and SoundGroups cannot be added while the game is running.

searchDocs.title: 2. Start the client​
searchDocs.content: In a client script, the setup is very similar:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.InitClient() -- Yields until the schema is ready. -- The schema can be used from here on.   InitClient asks the server for the schema and then preloads the sounds you tagged for preloading. You can pass a timeout for that preload as its first argument.  danger Call InitServer once on the server and InitClient once on each client. Do not call them more than once.

searchDocs.title: 3. Use it from other scripts​
searchDocs.content: Most functions in the library throw an error when they are used before the schema is ready. Any script that is not the one that started the library should wait for the schema first:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) VluxySF.Startup.WaitForSchema() -- Yields until the schema is ready. -- The schema can be used from here on.   If you do not want your script to yield, use ConnectForSchema:  VluxySF.Startup.ConnectForSchema(function() VluxySF.FetchPlayOnce("LoFiBeat1") end) -- This line runs right away.   tip If you are certain your code runs after the schema is loaded, you do not need to wait at all. VluxySF.Startup.IsInitialized() tells you whether it is ready.

searchDocs.title: Advanced: start it from a module loader​
searchDocs.content: If your game loads its modules in phases, like Init and then Start, you can start VluxySF during Init. Everything that runs on Start or later can then use the schema without waiting.  You have to bring your own module loader for this. This is commonly called a single script architecture.  Server module that starts the library:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local soundFolder = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild("SOUNDS") local Orchestrator = {} function Orchestrator.Init() VluxySF.Startup.InitServer(soundFolder) end function Orchestrator.Start() -- The schema can be used here. end return Orchestrator   Client module that starts the library:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local Orchestrator = {} function Orchestrator.Init() VluxySF.Startup.InitClient() -- Yields until the schema is ready. end function Orchestrator.Start() -- The schema can be used here. end return Orchestrator   Any other module:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local VluxySF = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.VluxySF) local MyModule = {} function MyModule.Start() -- The schema can be used here, without WaitForSchema. end return MyModule   note This only works if your loader finishes every Init before it runs any Start. Sub modules can use the schema too, as long as they run on Start or after.

searchDocs.title: Next step​
searchDocs.content: The library is running. Continue to Examples to start playing sounds.

searchDocs.title: SoundDefinitions​
searchDocs.content: </> type SoundDefinitions = {[string]: SoundDefinition} A dictionary of sound names for fetching SoundDefinitions.

searchDocs.title: SoundDefinition​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SoundDefinition { Properties: SoundSerialized-- Properties of the sound. Effects: SoundChildrenSerialized-- Individual SoundEffects and their Properties. EffectsCount: number-- Amount of SoundEffects in the SoundDefinition. } Fully Serialized Sound.

searchDocs.title: Combine​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundPresets.Combine( ...: (Sound ) → ()-- Your Preset Closures to combine. ) → (Sound ) → ()-- Closure of the combined presets. Combines presets together into 1 reusable preset. INFO Presets are applied in sequence from first to last. local myCombinedPreset = SoundPresets.Combine( SoundPresets.NaturalPlaybackJitter(0.8, 0.1), SoundPresets.NaturalVolumeJitter(0.7, 0.15) ) local myCombinedPreset2 = SoundPresets.Combine( myCombinedPreset, SoundPresets.Parent(workspace.Sounds) ) local sound1 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound1", nil, myCombinedPreset) local sound2 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound2", nil, myCombinedPreset) local sound3 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound3", nil, myCombinedPreset2) local sound4 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound4", nil, myCombinedPreset2)

searchDocs.title: Parent​
searchDocs.content: </> SoundPresets.Parent( parent: Instance -- The parent to set the sound too. ) → (Sound ) → ()-- Closure of the preset. Sets the parent of a sound. local myPreset = SoundPresets.Parent(workspace.Sounds) local sound1 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound1", nil, myPreset) local sound2 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound2", nil, myPreset) local sound3 = VluxySF.Fetch("mySound3", nil, myPreset)
